records.query: Summarize the key safety measures and operational considerations that distinguish hot refueling procedures for Navy aircraft at Air Force bases from standard refueling practices.

The refueling process must be stopped immediately if tank overpressure indicator lights illuminate or if the fuel dump valve is not closed. Equipment must use API Bulletin 1529 Type C Grade 2 hose with the specified couplings, ferrules and nozzles, with pressurized serviceability inspections every 24 hours or after maintenance. records.answer: Open-air refueling: The Fuel Servicing Safety Zone (FSSZ) is the area within 50 feet of a pressurized fuel-carrying servicing component (servicing hose, fuel nozzle, SPR, hydrant hose cart, ramp hydrant connection point, etc.) and 25 feet around aircraft fuel vent outlets; it applies to open ramps and to the insides of hangars and shelters approved for fuel servicing. Refueling will not start until all nonessential personnel and equipment are removed from the servicing area, and restrictions apply to entry of nonessential personnel or equipment. The FSSZ must be strictly enforced when one or more aircraft are parked in a HAS/PAS. Powered support equipment should be positioned outside the shelter when possible; if it must be inside, all aircraft entry doors must remain open. records.query: Explain the components and design of the AFTF.
records.reference: The AFTF (Aircraft Fire Training Facility) is a fixed site simulator for realistic aircraft fire suppression training. records.query: Summarize the procedures and safety requirements for removing, packaging, and handling wet and dry batteries from vehicles; mention hazard precautions as well.
records.reference: Wet batteries (except nickel, iron-alkaline) must be removed from vehicles and reported as excess, kept charged, and maintained in a charged condition while awaiting disposal instructions. Dry batteries should be space packaged and packed in accordance with Specification PPP-B-140, with vent holes sealed. Battery posts must be protected using plastic caps or tape conforming to Specification SAE AMS-T-22085. Wet batteries may remain installed in vehicles during military aircraft transport if protected against short circuits by disconnecting and securing cables away from terminals, and properly secured to prevent acid leakage. Dry batteries pose no special hazard and may be installed in the vehicle or shipped with OVE without additional precautions. Wet batteries received with vehicles may be used until the first exercise is completed, after which they must be transferred to a battery room, kept charged, and either shipped or replaced with dry batteries. Dry batteries, whether received charged or not, can be stored in the vehicle’s battery carrier, though indoor storage is preferred, and their vent holes must be sealed until activation. Cable terminals should be greased and taped according to military specifications, and dry batteries must not be activated unless no serviceable wet battery is available. Hazard precautions include preventing acid leakage and short circuits for wet batteries, and ensuring proper handling and activation procedures for dry batteries to avoid chemical exposure.

Nickel-iron-alkaline batteries are discharged to 0.5 V per cell, short-circuited with wires connected, and may be received discharged, dumped of electrolyte and short-circuited. Dry batteries are packaged and packed in accordance with the overseas requirements of PPP-B-140, and their filler-cap vent holes must be plugged or sealed. Electrolyte is packaged and packed per O-S-801 and stowed where it can be easily removed at ports when maritime regulations require special stowing; packaged batteries and electrolyte are stowed with other OVE. Battery posts are covered with plastic caps or tape conforming to SAE AMS-T-22085; cable connectors are preserved, packaged per MIL-STD-2073-1 and secured in the battery compartment or stored with the removed battery; batteries left in place are covered with waterproofed protective paper (PPP-B-1055) extending down the sides and ends at least 6 inches and secured with pressure-sensitive tape. Wet batteries may be shipped in military aircraft only if cables are removed, ends secured away from terminals, and the battery is secured so acid leakage will not occur; dry batteries may be installed in the carrier or placed with OVE. records.query: List the processes in included in the Equipment Painting and list the precautions to be considered during surface painting.

records.query: What are the procedures for installing, removing, and requisitioning vehicle markings, including reflective tape?
records.reference: Vehicle markings, including reflective tape, are installed by cleaning the surface, removing the liner, positioning the tape, and applying firm pressure. For removal, pressure-sensitive tape can be softened with heat and isopropyl alcohol (TT-I-735), while older tape requires paint remover (TT-R-2918) or 3M decal remover disks. Markings can be requisitioned through DLA Document Services Online. If decals are unavailable and safety is impacted, stenciling is permitted. Reflectors follow drawing B161059, mounted 24–60 inches above the ground, visible at 100 feet. Install tape according to the steps; damaged areas may be patched.
records.answer:
Installing reflectorized tape (TO 36-1-191, para 2.88): clean the vehicle surface before applying the marking; remove the liner film; position the emblem and tack it in place with thumb pressure; starting in the center, use hard overlapping strokes of a low-friction plastic squeegee, then re-squeegee the edges with very firm strokes; apply clean sealer to the tape edges; repairs to damaged areas can be made without stripping the original tape by cleaning the damaged area and applying new tape over it.

Removing reflectorized tape (para 2.89): WARNING: lacquer thinner, kylol, and isopropyl alcohol are flammable and toxic; good general ventilation is normally adequate; skin and eye protection is required; avoid all sources of ignition; failure to comply could result in injury, death, or long-term health hazards. Routine removal: soften the tape with heat (heat lamp, heat gun, steam, etc.) and soften adhesive residue with isopropyl alcohol-soaked rags (TT-1-735), scraping away with a plastic scraper or putty knife. Old tape: mask off the surrounding area and brush paint remover (TT-R-2918, Type) over the tape, reapplying at short intervals and removing residue with a plastic scraper or bevel-edge putty knife between applications; the remover may damage the paint beneath, requiring cleaning and touch-up painting. Alternative: a 4 or 6 inch stripe, molding and decal remover disk (3M) removes tape without damaging paint; disks are NSN 5130-01-390-9503 (4 inch) and NSN 5130-01-390-9504 (6 inch), with a drill adapter NSN 5130-01-391-2095.

Requisitioning markings (para 2.90): all markings in the chapter are requisitioned through DLA Document Services via the Document Services Online (DSO) website; once an account is created, orders are processed through the Travis Plant. DLA Document Services: (707) 424-0770/(707) 424-4537, DSN 837. If decals are not immediately available and the unmarked equipment hampers mission capability or presents a safety hazard, appropriate markings may be stenciled on the vehicle or equipment until decals are received.

records.query: What caution is taken into consideration while using high-pressure wash equipment, and explain the function of the portable, 45-gallon, foam-generating cleaning unit?
records.reference: When using high-pressure wash equipment, caution must be taken to ensure it is never used on aircraft landing gear and components, wheels, and brakes, as it can force lubricants out of bearings and attachment points, causing corrosion and wear problems. The function of the portable, 45-gallon, foam-generating cleaning unit is to dispense foam. This cleaning unit is a simplified, portable, pressure-operated, foam-dispensing system that uses the available air supply as its power source to force cleaning solution into the hose and create foam.
records.answer: Caution: High pressure wash equipment which develops more than 175 PSI nozzle pressure shall not be used to apply cleaning compounds unless specifically authorized by the equipment System Program Manager (SPM); high pressure can cause cleaning compounds to become entrapped in enclosed areas causing corrosion, and high pressure wash equipment shall never be used on aircraft landing gear and components, wheels, and brakes as it can force lubricants out of bearings and attach points and cause corrosion and wear problems. Use only 40 degree flat fan spray nozzles and keep the nozzle stand-off distance at least 12 inches. Portable 45-gallon foam generating cleaning unit: a simplified, portable, pressure-operated foam-dispensing system that uses available air supply as its power source without pumps; air is metered directly into the pressurized solution chamber, which forces cleaning solution into the hose to create foam. Apply the foam, let it dwell at least one minute without drying, then scrub with a cleaning kit, brush, or cloth and rinse. Note: the pages give the nozzle type as 400 in one place and 40 degree in another; 40 degree flat fan is cited in the TO 1-1-700 pages.

records.query: Define CSO and list down the activities performed in the presence of CSS.
records.reference: Concurrent Servicing Operations (CSO) are the simultaneous servicing of fuel and other aircraft operations such as munitions loading/unloading, aircraft reconfiguration, and aircraft -6 TO inspections. The CSS's activities include ensuring all non-essential personnel and equipment are cleared from the area, briefing team members on duties and emergency procedures, checking the status of the aircraft and its systems with the SCR, ensuring cabin crew have briefed passengers, directing and monitoring the positioning of support equipment and personnel, and having SPR/Vent monitors reposition aircraft wheel chocks as required.
